_disclaimer: PHQ-9 and GAD-7 item wording as published by their developers. BAYOU-NOVA is a proof of concept (2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge) and is not for clinical use.
scheduling_policy: NOT auto-scheduled. The platform never sets a schedule, sends a reminder or suggests a due date for these instruments. They are started only by the astronaut, or because a flight surgeon asked for one.
required_note: Administration frequency and interpretation in spaceflight context should follow guidance from your flight surgeon. These instruments are validated for general clinical populations.
permission: Developed by Drs. Robert L. Spitzer, Janet B.W. Williams, Kurt Kroenke and colleagues, with an educational grant from Pfizer Inc. No permission required to reproduce, translate, display or distribute.
wording_check: Item wording was checked in Phase 5 against a clinical reproduction of the forms, not the developers' own download page. Compare with the official PHQ Screeners copy before any public release.

difficulty_item.prompt: If you checked off any problems, how difficult have these problems made it for you to do your work, take care of things at home, or get along with other people?

instruments.name: Patient Health Questionnaire-9
instruments.measures: Depression symptom severity over the last 2 weeks
instruments.label: Validated clinical instrument — Kroenke K, Spitzer RL, Williams JBW. The PHQ-9: validity of a brief depression severity measure. J Gen Intern Med. 2001;16(9):606-613.
instruments.validated_in: Primary care and obstetrics-gynaecology patients on Earth. Not validated in astronauts or in spaceflight.
instruments.stem: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by any of the following problems?
items: Little interest or pleasure in doing things
Trouble falling or staying asleep, or sleeping too much
Feeling tired or having little energy
Feeling bad about yourself, or that you are a failure or have let yourself or your family down
Trouble concentrating on things, such as reading the newspaper or watching television
Moving or speaking so slowly that other people could have noticed. Or the opposite: being so fidgety or restless that you have been moving around a lot more than usual
Thoughts that you would be better off dead, or of hurting yourself in some way
instruments.bands_source: Published severity bands (scores of 5, 10, 15 and 20) from Kroenke, Spitzer and Williams 2001.
instruments.spaceflight_overlap_note: Several items (sleep, energy, appetite, concentration) describe things that spaceflight itself commonly changes, so a score may read differently in flight than in the clinic populations the bands were built on.

layer1_item.note: Any answer above 'Not at all' on item 9 is treated as a Layer 1 red flag, whatever the total score.

instruments.name: Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7
instruments.measures: Anxiety symptom severity over the last 2 weeks
instruments.label: Validated clinical instrument — Spitzer RL, Kroenke K, Williams JBW, Löwe B. A brief measure for assessing generalized anxiety disorder: the GAD-7. Arch Intern Med. 2006;166(10):1092-1097.
instruments.validated_in: Primary care patients on Earth. Not validated in astronauts or in spaceflight.
instruments.stem: Over the last 2 weeks, how often have you been bothered by any of the following problems?
items: Feeling nervous, anxious, or on edge
Not being able to stop or control worrying
Worrying too much about different things
Being so restless that it's hard to sit still
Feeling afraid as if something awful might happen
instruments.bands_source: Published cut points (scores of 5, 10 and 15) from Spitzer, Kroenke, Williams and Löwe 2006.
instruments.spaceflight_overlap_note: Restlessness, irritability and trouble relaxing can also follow from confinement, workload or poor sleep in flight, so a score may read differently than in the clinic populations the cut points were built on.
